text:
Maya Singh: opening thread for ACME ticket — customer seeing intermittent 502/504s hitting hosted inference endpoint since last cert rotation :frowning:
ACME Integrations: seeing spikes of ~20% 502s from our EU clients starting ~2024-11-04 07:15 UTC, started after auto rotation window, can reproduce with a steady curl loop
Maya Singh: can you paste a curl sample and any headers? also what region/endpoint?
ACME Integrations: endpoint: https://api.redwood-hosted.com/v1/generate (eu-west-1). curl -v output attached
ACME Integrations: ```
$ for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://api.redwood-hosted.com/v1/generate; sleep 0.2; done
200 0.122
200 0.128
502 0.045
200 0.130
502 0.047
``` 
Maya Singh: thanks. @alex can you check edge health and cert rotation logs around 07:00-08:00 UTC? suspecting some intermediate resolver or CDN mismatch
Alex Turner: looking. I see a cert rotation job at 07:03 pushed new chain to edge-pop fleet. No immediate errors in the rollout logs. But the gateway LB started returning 502 from some PoPs at 07:08. Adding tracing now.
Jonah Park: throwing in runtime traces — any differences in SNI on backend connections? we sometimes see SNI mismatch when upstream uses old certs
Alex Turner: initial traces show backend upstream (edge-proxy -> origin) TCP established but TLS handshake stalls 30s then resets for a subset of client IPs. handshake timeout path: likely resolver returning wrong A records intermittently.
Priya Nair: can ACME run an openssl test and dig from affected client nets? Need server_name, cipher info.
ACME Integrations: running openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-hosted.com:443 -servername api.redwood-hosted.com -debug
ACME Integrations: ```
CONNECTED(00000003)
140736828...: SSL handshake has read 0 bytes and written 318 bytes
139...: get_peer_certificates: peer did not return certificates
---
No client certificate CA names sent
---
write:errno=104
``` 
ACME Integrations: also saw intermittent SERVFAILs from their resolver when doing dig +time=2 api.redwood-hosted.com @8.8.8.8
ACME Integrations: ```
$ dig +short api.redwood-hosted.com @8.8.8.8
(works)
$ dig +short api.redwood-hosted.com @1.1.1.1
(works)
$ dig +short api.redwood-hosted.com @their-corp-resolver
<no answer> ;; SERVFAIL
``` 
Maya Singh: ok that's useful — suggests customer-side resolver flapping but they also reported clients on multiple ISPs. Could be EDNS/UDP fragmentation or authoritative returning mixed records during rotation
Alex Turner: checking authoritative DNS logs — we did a staggered zone publish to add a new ALIAS for the rotated edge cert CNAME between 07:00-07:05. I see high RTTs from a subset of resolvers and a handful of AXFR errors. I'm pulling authoritative logs now.
Jonah Park: also saw a spike of TLS handshake retransmits and occasional client hello without SNI (weird) from older HTTP clients. When the resolver returns older A record that points at legacy-cdn, that CDN's edge hasn't got the new cert chain yet causing handshake failures -> 502 from gateway.
Priya Nair: reproduction plan: 1) force DNS to a resolver that returns legacy A; 2) run openssl s_client and curl to show handshake fails; 3) traceroute to see which PoP is returned
Maya Singh: @ACME can you run a traceroute and share a packet capture if possible from an affected client? That helps confirm path-level fragmentation
ACME Integrations: traceroute shows hop through carrier-proxy then the edge PoP 52.x.y.z which corresponds to eu-west-pop-3. pcap attached (we'll DM)
Alex Turner: confirmed — eu-west-pop-3 had delayed config push for ~90s during the rotation window due to a transient orchestration lock. Most traffic targeted to that pop would get a backend with old cert until config applied -> handshake timeout.
Jonah Park: that explains subset failures. But why would resolvers direct clients to that pop sporadically? TTLs were 30s during rotation, some resolvers are ignoring TTL and returning cached A linked to deprecated LB.
Priya Nair: mitigation suggestions: 1) temporarily increase edge LB health-check sensitivity to drop hosts without new cert; 2) revert to previous cert chain if rotation still incomplete; 3) raise DNS TTL next rotation to give more time/trickle config (counterintuitive but we can pre-warm) 4) advise customers to use resilient resolvers
Maya Singh: immediate action: Alex, can you force drain on nodes without new cert and push missing config to eu-west-pop-3? Jonah can add a fallback route to other PoPs for the customer while we remediate
Alex Turner: draining nodes without matching certs now. Pushing config to eu-west-pop-3 — ETA 90s. I'll also mark the rotation job as failed so cron won't continue rollouts.
deploy-bot: deploy started by Alex Turner (deploy/edge-config) — job id d-20241104-713
Jonah Park: adding temporary routing rule for ACME API path to prefer eu-west-pop-1/2 for the next 30m
Maya Singh: @ACME can you confirm if 502 rate drops after 2-3 minutes? also can you switch their clients to 8.8.8.8 as a test to rule out corp resolver flapping
ACME Integrations: switching to 8.8.8.8 for some clients now. will report back in 2 min
ACME Integrations: quick update — spike dropped to ~1% within 90s after your pushes. curl loop now shows no 502s. thanks, looks like it's improving :relieved:
Maya Singh: great. follow-ups: Alex - postmortem with timeline and root cause (partial config push + DNS TTL + orchestration lock). Jonah - consider adding pre-checks to rotation job that verify PoP config before DNS changes. Priya - add diagnostics to runtime to map handshake failures to PoP/cert version for faster triage
Alex Turner: noted. I'll open incident (ENG-EDGE-4123) with logs and link to deploy job. Will include mitigation steps we executed and checklist for next rotation
Jonah Park: Also recommend temporarily increasing DNS authoritative SOA serial propagation window and staggering CNAME flips with health-check gating
Maya Singh: I'm going to update ACME ticket with mitigation steps and ask them to keep using 8.8.8.8 for now until next rotation. Thanks all — closing thread once postmortem launched :thumbsup:
ACME Integrations: thanks everyone! major thanks to @Maya and SRE team :clap:
Maya Singh: closing notes: takeaway — cert rotation needs gated rollout: ensure PoP config applied and cert present before changing DNS/CNAMEs, and avoid low TTLs during active rollout. We'll document in runbook.
